observations.text: Re-review delta at 8be4e4d, tree clean (git status --porcelain 0 lines). Mechanical selection: argv 'git diff --name-only 42a821a..8be4e4d', exit 0, stdout = crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_icon_rail.rs plus six docs/feature/nav-quick-actions files (acceptance.md/.html, architecture.md/.html, handoff.json, runs/review.oracle.S1.json); stderr empty. Exactly one test file changed and it is the one both findings named; crates/foundry-acceptance/tests/features/nav-quick-actions.feature, src/steps/feature_nav_quick_actions.rs, src/lib.rs, the two migrated oracles and every production file are byte-unchanged, so the judgments recorded for P1, P2, P3, L1-L4, L6 and the migration survey are retained unexamined.

The oracle correction is the stronger of the two remediations offered, and it is the whole correction. feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:53 EVERY_OPERATOR grows from 4 to 7 names: Home, Board, Teams, Invite a member, Machine tokens, Settings, Keyboard shortcuts, with FOR_A_WORKSPACE_ADMIN, FOR_AN_INSTANCE_ADMIN and ALWAYS_LAST untouched, so the owed set per rights row becomes 8, 9, 9 and 10 members. Nothing else in the file changed: owed_destinations at :837 and the sorted assert_eq at :877-881 are untouched, and the offered side still comes from support/rail_reading.rs:74. The added doc comment refuses the derive-from-the-page alternative for the right reason - 'a rail compared only against the page it is drawn from agrees with itself even when both lose a destination' - so the lane keeps an independent oracle rather than a tautological one. No other module references EVERY_OPERATOR.

P4 now has a measured semantic RED of its own, which it did not have at 42a821a. Browser lane at 8be4e4d (cargo build --release -p foundry-app, then FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=nav-collapse-icon-rail FOUNDRY_XTASK_INCLUDE_DOCKER=1 cargo test -p foundry-acceptance --test acceptance in the Lima VM; log scratchpad nqa-rail.log): '17 scenarios (2 passed, 15 failed), 94 steps (79 passed, 15 failed)', 'acceptance run failed: 15 step(s) failed, 0 parsing error(s), 0 hook error(s)', exit 101. Every one of the 15 failures is the missing behaviour. Fourteen are the owed-set mismatch in four rights shapes, e.g. 'the rail announces [Board, Home, Keyboard shortcuts, Settings, Sign out] where her rights give her [Board, Home, Invite a member, Keyboard shortcuts, Machine tokens, Settings, Sign out, Teams]', across the open desk nav, the narrow rail, the no-script arm, the restored-choice arm and the three phone widths. The fifteenth is the keyboard walk: 'walking the page with the Tab key never stopped on [Teams, Invite a member, Machine tokens] ... reached [7] of her 10 destinations', which is a direct falsifier for expectation E8.

That RED is semantic, not BROKEN, including the four failures that land on a Given. Each of those four is the shipped arrange-and-check Given at feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:126 (nav-collapse-icon-rail.feature:69), whose panic is the same membership mismatch with the full member reading attached, not a harness, browser, container or sign-in failure: 79 of 94 steps passed, every browser session, Postgres container and sign-in completed, and the run reports 0 parsing errors and 0 hook errors. The four shapes correspond one-to-one to the four rights rows, so L5's enumerated cases each fail for the promised reason. The 2 passing scenarios exercise paths that do not call the rail-membership helper and pin already-shipped behaviour, so they are not vacuous passes of the new law.

The design record now matches the code, so the paired non-blocking finding is answered in the artifact and not only in prose. The decision text reads 'P4 adds no browser scenario, but its lane is MIGRATED, not inherited unchanged', citing :53-56, :837 and :877-881 and the offered-only reading at rail_reading.rs:74; a new Impact row 'acceptance-oracle crates/foundry-acceptance/src/steps/feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:53 Migrated' is present beside the unchanged rail_reading.rs row and records that the first survey stopped at the reading support; a matching Agreement consumer row names it the one consumer that encodes the member LIST rather than the member SHAPE; the refuted-assumption list gains 'The shipped icon-rail lane quantifies over the members it reads' with its counterevidence; L5's treatment text and the acceptance row both now name the migrated owed set instead of an unchanged lane. The feature_nav_icon_rail.rs support is also declared in the Supports list of this bundle, so it is in scope as a reviewed support rather than an outside file.

Reuse justified at the new commit for the fast-lane RED, with no new execution claimed. The fast lane was last executed at 42a821a (10 scenarios, 2 passed, 8 failed, recorded above). Between 42a821a and 8be4e4d the only changed test file is feature_nav_icon_rail.rs, a disjoint step module: no step phrase of nav-quick-actions.feature is defined in it, its only changed symbol is the EVERY_OPERATOR constant used solely by icon-rail steps, and the production sources, the oracle, its supports and the Lima runtime are byte-identical. A compile regression is excluded by execution rather than by reading: the 8be4e4d browser run built and ran the same test binary. The fast-lane result is therefore reused, not restamped. Capability limits unchanged: typesafe unavailable (TYPESAFE_API_KEY absent), and this review executed no test of its own.

diagnostic: ACCEPTED at 8be4e4d. Both findings of the 42a821a round are resolved in the artifacts, and the delta introduces no new defect. Oracle finding: feature_nav_icon_rail.rs:53 EVERY_OPERATOR now names Teams, Invite a member and Machine tokens beside Home, Board, Settings and Keyboard shortcuts, so the owed set is 8, 9, 9 and 10 members across the four rights rows; owed_destinations and the sorted equality are untouched, and the authored owed set keeps the lane an independent oracle rather than one that reads its expectation back from the page it measures - the comment states that anti-tautology reason itself. Design finding: the P4 decision text, a new Migrated Impact row and matching Agreement row, a new refuted assumption with its locators, L5's treatment text and the acceptance row all now say MIGRATED instead of inherited unchanged, and the support is declared in Supports. P4 gained the falsifier it lacked: the browser lane at 8be4e4d fails 15 of 17 scenarios, every failure the missing behaviour - fourteen owed-set mismatches in four rights shapes across the open desk nav, the narrow rail, the no-script arm, the restored-choice arm and 320/390/480 px, plus the keyboard walk that never stops on the three names, which falsifies E8 directly - with 0 parsing errors, 0 hook errors and 79 of 94 steps passing, so the four failures that land on the shipped arrange-and-check Given are semantic, not BROKEN. The fast-lane RED recorded at 42a821a is reused on a justified comparison: the only changed test file is a disjoint step module whose single changed symbol no nav-quick-actions step reads, and the 8be4e4d browser run proves the shared binary still builds; no new execution is claimed. Every unaffected judgment of the first round stands: P1, P2 and P3 keep their constructible public oracle and measured business RED, L1-L4 and L6 close in both directions, and the .actions and Slice-09 migrations remain complete. Craft may proceed. Completion obligations, unchanged and unmet by design at this phase: implementation GREEN on the nav-quick-actions lane, cargo xtask check-arch for T1, and the icon-rail lane re-run with FOUNDRY_ACCEPTANCE_TAGS=nav-collapse-icon-rail FOUNDRY_XTASK_INCLUDE_DOCKER=1 - P4 runtime stays unobserved until that lane is reported, and a green gate on a Docker-less host is not that evidence. Residue retained: widths below 320 px, short desk viewports, what an assistive technology actually announces, and the pwa phone row that measures Home and Board on one wrapping row. typesafe unavailable; this review executed no test.
